_comment: What `harness sync` may write and what it must never touch. Everything not listed as owned is left exactly as found.

claude.output_style: Owned conditionally, from the `voice` stance rather than from the template: a variant with a file in claude/output-styles/ installs that style, a variant mapped to a Claude Code built-in style (today only `concise`, mapped to `Concise`) installs that style by name, a variant with neither installs none and removes the style a previous selection installed. Ownership is what the reconciliation journal records having been written, never the style's name, so a value the harness did not write — including one it also ships — is the user's and is never rewritten, removed or reported as drift.
claude.allow_rules: every entry in settings.template.json permissions.allow, merged as a set; entries the user added are kept; an entry a previous template added and this one dropped is removed
claude.agents: every file in claude/agents/, linked into ~/.claude/agents/
claude.hook_ids_note: Each id names a policy under policy/hooks/ and the lifecycle event it answers on. Registration is not per id: sync registers one coordinator command per event, so `stance`/`variant` say when a policy acts inside dispatch, never whether it is registered.
claude.commands: every file in claude/commands/, linked into ~/.claude/commands/

native_telemetry._comment: Written only while telemetry.native is true, and owned one variable at a time: every other variable in env is the user's and is never read, changed or removed. A managed key already holding a value the harness did not write is reported and left alone.

workspaces._comment: Written only while workspaces_dir is set, and owned by the native_telemetry rules: a value equal to the harness's is taken over, a different one is reported and left, and on unset a key is taken back out only when the reconciliation journal holds it.

native_telemetry._comment: Written only while telemetry.native is true. The [otel] table is reconciled as one key, so keys the user set in it are carried through; exporter and metrics_exporter are the two the harness sets. No header is ever written: Codex takes a literal header map in config.toml and offers no environment or command indirection for it.
